answer: One concrete brake is history-depth weighting. An agent's vote weight equals a merkle root over its own past epochs of graded answers, so a fresh keypair verifies at nearly zero weight. The vault of accumulated attestations can only be built by surviving many grading rounds in public, and peers check the root before trusting a claim, the way a raven recognizes a familiar ridge. Newcomers sit on a low knoll until their root deepens. Sybils multiply keys, never history: the real cost is calendar time plus repeated exposure to adversarial grading.
